climate.overview_html: The Climate Action Tracker now projects 2.7°C of warming by 2100 under current policies, up from 2.6°C a year ago. At COP31, finance talks remain unresolved as a Brazilian analysis puts the gap to the $1.3tn annual goal at $840bn. A UN-backed initiative launched guidance on AI-generated climate information.

items.headline: Climate Action Tracker raises its current-policy warming estimate to 2.7°C
items.summary: The median 2100 projection rose from 2.6°C, with a range of 2.2-3.4°C. CAT expects warming to pass 1.5°C around 2030; Inside Climate News reports action has stalled for a fifth year.

items.headline: COP31 finance talks stall with an $840bn annual gap to the $1.3tn goal
items.summary: The presidency circulated a first outline of a political declaration, but finance and fossil fuels remain open. Parties are also split over the baseline for tripling adaptation finance and over predictable loss-and-damage funding.

items.headline: UN, UNESCO and Brazil issue guidance on AI-generated climate information
items.summary: The Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change launched the guidance at COP31 in Antalya.

major_events.name: Bay of Bengal low, India
major_events.status: Low over SE Bay; may reach cyclone
major_events.impact: The low formed on Nov 13 and is expected to strengthen over the weekend while moving NW, then NNW. Fishermen are barred from parts of the Bay until Nov 17; heavy rain is likely in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and showers in Tamil Nadu.

major_events.name: Cape York heatwave, Queensland
major_events.status: Extreme warning; easing late next week
major_events.impact: Weipa has had 39 straight days above 36°C and a November record of 39.8°C. Severe heatwave warnings run from the Gulf Country to the Whitsundays.

major_events.name: Storms in northern Italy
major_events.status: Red alert lowered to orange Nov 13
major_events.impact: Rivers flooded at Massa, Fivizzano and La Spezia, with landslides in Lunigiana. Orange alerts covered parts of Liguria, Emilia-Romagna, Tuscany, Umbria and Lazio on Nov 13.

major_events.name: St. Johns River flooding, Florida
major_events.impact: The river above Lake Harney was 9.1 ft and rising on Nov 11, with a crest of 9.7-10.3 ft forecast near major flood level. Downstream reaches crest about three days later.

major_events.name: Cold weekend, eastern US
major_events.impact: After storms with two tornadoes near Philadelphia on Nov 12 and a rainy nor'easter on Nov 13, weekend lows fall into the 30s°F in NYC, Philadelphia and DC, with snow possible in the Alleghenies.

weather.overview_html: The Bay of Bengal low could reach cyclone strength as it tracks northwest this weekend. In Queensland, Weipa has logged 39 straight days above 36°C and a November record of 39.8°C. Italy's storms eased to orange alerts on Nov 13 after river floods in Tuscany and Liguria, while two tornadoes struck the Philadelphia area in a rare November outbreak.

items.headline: Weipa sets a November record of 39.8°C in a 39-day heatwave
items.summary: The Cape York town has logged 39 consecutive days above 36°C. An extreme heatwave warning covers the peninsula, with severe warnings from the Gulf Country to the Whitsundays until late next week.

items.headline: Bay of Bengal low may intensify into a cyclone this weekend
items.summary: The low formed on Friday under an Andaman Sea circulation and should strengthen while moving northwest, then north-northwest toward the central Bay. Fishermen are told to stay out of parts of the Bay until Nov 17.

items.headline: Italy lowers storm alerts to orange after floods in Tuscany and Liguria
items.summary: The Frigido flooded at Massa, the Bardine at Fivizzano and the Lagora at La Spezia. In Ventimiglia, 19 migrants and one Italian were rescued after a river surge swept them away.

items.headline: AccuWeather calls the eastern Pacific hurricane season over after 25 named storms
items.summary: The season produced 25 named storms and 11 major hurricanes, which AccuWeather ties to the strong El Niño. It called the end before the official Nov 30 close.

items.headline: Two tornadoes and large hail hit the Philadelphia region
items.summary: A line of Thursday afternoon storms brought heavy hail to Delaware County, damaged buildings, and prompted an NWS damage survey in Burlington County, NJ.

items.headline: SAWS warns of heat and veld-fire risk in Gauteng, Northern Cape and Free State
items.summary: The warning ran until Nov 13. SAWS links the heat to the strong El Niño and expects below-normal rainfall for October-December.

renewables.overview_html: WindEurope reports 8.8 GW of wind added in Europe in the first half, up 30%, and expects about 24 GW for the year. Britain's grid operator issued a margin notice on Nov 8 during a third straight day of low wind, its seventh of 2026. Vestas narrowed its 2026 guidance after offshore project costs cut its quarterly profit.

items.headline: Europe added 8.8 GW of wind in the first half, up 30% on 2025
items.summary: WindEurope expects about 24 GW of installations in 2026, a record. It says decisions on permitting, the EU grids package and a binding 2040 renewables target will set the pace after that.

items.headline: Vestas narrows 2026 guidance after a weaker third quarter
items.summary: Q3 revenue rose 6% to €5.68bn, but EBIT before special items of €483m missed the €526m consensus on higher costs at a European offshore project. Revenue guidance is now €20.5-21.5bn and shares fell about 7.7%.

items.headline: NESO issues an electricity margin notice during a three-day wind lull
items.summary: The notice covered 6-11am on Nov 9 and flagged a 1,388 MW shortfall against an 808 MW contingency requirement. NESO cancelled it at 09:11; it was the seventh such notice of 2026, against one in all of 2025.

science.overview_html: Google's PARDIG preprint describes an AI precipitation reanalysis trained on GPM radar retrievals, now feeding WeatherNext 3. A NeurIPS paper finds satellite-only front detection reaches a CSI of 0.402, within the range of agreement between agencies. In Nature Climate Change, every IPCC region had reached 90-94% of its 1.5°C-equivalent warming by the end of 2025.

items.headline: PARDIG learns global 15-minute precipitation from sparse satellite retrievals
items.summary: The model is trained on GPM CORRA radar-radiometer retrievals and outputs 0.1° rainfall every 15 minutes, in a near-real-time version from 2016 and a 1999-2023 record. The authors say it also improves WeatherNext 3 forecasts; the data is CC BY 4.0.

items.headline: Satellite-only ML front detection scores close to reanalysis-based methods
items.summary: Using only geostationary infrared imagery, the detector reaches CSI@150 km of 0.402, within the spread of agreement among met agencies. Adding 28 ERA5 variables helps most where near-surface wind and moisture matter.

items.headline: All IPCC regions have reached 90-94% of their 1.5°C-equivalent warming
items.meta: Li, Zwiers, Zhang, Sun · Nature Climate Change
items.summary: Canada and much of Europe have already warmed more than 2°C, and some high-latitude regions more than 2.5°C. The authors project all regions reach 1.5°C-equivalent levels around 2029.

items.headline: State of the Climate report logs records in sea level, ocean heat and greenhouse gases
items.summary: Sea level, ocean heat content, Greenland ice loss, glacier thinning and the three main greenhouse gas concentrations all set records. Ocean surface pH fell to 8.050.

items.title: Google DeepMind opens SatWeave and PARDIG, the datasets behind WeatherNext 3
items.body_html: DeepMind released two datasets free on Google Cloud: SatWeave, an hourly 17-channel global image built from five geostationary satellites at about 10 km, and PARDIG, a 15-minute global rainfall estimate trained on NASA GPM radar. DeepMind says PARDIG detects light-to-moderate rain over 30% better than IMERG-Final. Both are free inputs that compete with paid satellite and precipitation products.

items.title: ICEYE to supply flood and wildfire monitoring to Poland's civil security hub
items.body_html: ICEYE signed a contract with the Polish Academy of Sciences Space Research Centre to deliver its Flood Solutions Suite, river-ice monitoring and a wildfire pilot to CS Hub PL, Poland's node in ESA's Space Resilience Nodes. Access is an always-on subscription for the State Fire Service, crisis teams and hydrological services, with no activation needed in an emergency.

items.title: Court ruling on Saildrone's Navy MUSV bid limits the Navy's OTA funding
items.body_html: The Court of Federal Claims found the Navy evaluated Saildrone’s MUSV proposal unfairly against Sea Machines and ordered a re-evaluation within 60 days. USNI News reports the ruling also gives the court jurisdiction over OTA protests and restricts how much of the $2.1B programme can be committed. Blue Water Autonomy's protest was denied.

items.title: ICE plans 15 European wind-output futures for launch on Dec 14
items.body_html: ICE will list 15 cash-settled wind futures settling on ENWEX wind-generation indices for Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and the UK, pending regulatory approval. ICE says the seven markets hold over 70% of Europe's installed wind capacity. Settlement on generation indices gives wind-output forecasters a direct traded benchmark.

items.title: DTN names a new CFO, chief revenue officer and chief legal officer
items.body_html: DTN appointed Ran Geber as CFO, formerly a divisional CFO at Amdocs, along with Fernando Magnaghi as chief revenue officer and Heather Randall as chief legal officer, effective immediately. CEO Manuel Zepeda announced the changes.
